key_insight: Functional septorhinoplasty in persistent COVID-19-related smell loss was associated with measurable changes in brain olfactory-network activity, suggesting central neural plasticity alongside improved nasal airflow.
clinical_relevance: This imaging study supports the idea that improving odorant access to the olfactory epithelium may help normalize higher-order brain responses in some patients with long-lasting post-COVID smell dysfunction.
method: Prospective cohort of persistent COVID-19-related olfactory dysfunction patients
Psychophysical smell testing, nasal airflow measurement, and task-based fMRI before and 6 months after surgery
Whole-brain analysis mapped to anatomical and olfactory atlases
evidence_signal: Eight participants completed paired pre- and post-operative fMRI assessments, with correlations reported between brain activation changes and nasal airflow or olfactory score changes.
watch_item: Very small sample size limits generalizability, and the findings show association rather than proof that the surgery directly caused the observed brain changes.
paper_title: Functional plasticity of the olfactory network following functional septorhinoplasty in persistent COVID-19-related olfactory dysfunction: an fMRI study
